To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) we treat text summarization as a budgeted submodulator maximization problem, (2) we show, both theoretically as well as empirically that the greedy algorithm can efficiently approximate the solution to the budgeted sub-modular maximization problem within a constant factor of the optimal solution, and (3) we empirically show that this approach outperforms the best performing method in the DUC'2004 evaluation on ROUGE-1 score.
we propose to treat text summarization as a submodular maximisation problem, and that we show that a modified greedy algorithm is near optimal for solving the problem.

(1) we propose a novel approach for multi-document summarization based on submodular optimization; (2) we provide a new algorithm for solving the submodular optimization problem with a budget constraint, and derive new approximation bounds for this problem; (3) we demonstrate that our approach performs well on the multi-document summarization task, and outperforms the state-of-the-art methods.

submodular functions can be used to solve a variety of summarization problems, and the budgeted sub-modularity can provide a principled way to solve the summarization problems with a limited budget.
